FROM employee e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM project p
    WHERE p.Dnum = e.Dno
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM works_on w
          WHERE w.Essn = e.Ssn
            AND w.Pno = p.Pnumber
      )
);

SELECT AVG(e.Salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employee e
WHERE e.Ssn IN (
    SELECT wo.Essn
    FROM works_on wo
    JOIN employee emp ON wo.Essn = emp.Ssn
    JOIN project p ON wo.Pno = p.Pnumber
    WHERE emp.Dno = p.Dnum
    GROUP BY wo.Essn
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT wo.Pno) = (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM project p2
        WHERE p2.Dnum = emp.Dno
    )
);

WITH emp_dept AS (
    SELECT Ssn, Salary, Dno FROM employee
),
emp_worked AS (
    SELECT ed.Ssn, ed.Salary, ed.Dno,
           COUNT(DISTINCT w.Pno) AS worked_proj_cnt
    FROM emp_dept ed
    LEFT JOIN works_on w ON w.Essn = ed.Ssn
    LEFT JOIN project p ON p.Pno = w.Pno AND p.Dnum = ed.Dno
    GROUP BY ed.Ssn, ed.Salary, ed.Dno
),
dept_total AS (
    SELECT Dno, COUNT(DISTINCT Pno) AS total_proj_cnt
    FROM project
    GROUP BY Dno
)
SELECT AVG(ew.Salary) AS average_salary
FROM emp_worked ew
JOIN dept_total dt ON ew.Dno = dt.Dno
WHERE ew.worked_proj_cnt = dt.total_proj_cnt;

SELECT d.Dname, AVG(e.Salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employee e
JOIN department d ON e.Dno = d.Dnumber
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM project p
    WHERE p.Dnum = e.Dno
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM works_on w
          WHERE w.Essn = e.Ssn
            AND w.Pno = p.Pnumber
      )
)
GROUP BY d.Dname;

SELECT 
    e.Dno AS department_number,
    AVG(e.Salary) AS average_salary
FROM employee e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM project p
    WHERE p.Dnum = e.Dno
    AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM works_on w
        WHERE w.Essn = e.Ssn
        AND w.Pno = p.Pnumber
    )
)
GROUP BY e.Dno

WITH emp_projects AS (
    SELECT e.Ssn, e.Dno, e.Salary,
           COUNT(DISTINCT w.Pno) AS proj_count
    FROM employee e
    JOIN works_on w ON e.Ssn = w.Essn
    JOIN project p ON w.Pno = p.Pnumber AND p.Dnum = e.Dno
    GROUP BY e.Ssn, e.Dno, e.Salary
),
dept_project_counts AS (
    SELECT Dno, COUNT(*) AS total_proj
    FROM project
    GROUP BY Dno
)
SELECT AVG(ep.Salary) AS avg_salary
FROM emp_projects ep
JOIN dept_project_counts dpc ON ep.Dno = dpc.Dno
WHERE ep.proj_count = dpc.total_proj
GROUP BY ep.Dno;

WITH dept_proj AS (
    SELECT 
        D.Dname,
        P.Pname,
        SUM(W.Hours) AS total_hours,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY D.Dnumber ORDER BY SUM(W.Hours) DESC) AS rn
    FROM works_on W
    JOIN employee E ON W.Essn = E.Ssn
    JOIN department D ON E.Dno = D.Dnumber
    JOIN project P ON W.Pno = P.Pnumber
    GROUP BY D.Dnumber, P.Pnumber
)
SELECT Dname, Pname, total_hours
FROM dept_proj
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY Dname;

FROM works_on w
JOIN employee e ON w.Essn = e.Ssn
JOIN project p ON w.Pno = p.Pnumber
JOIN department d ON e.Dno = d.Dnumber
GROUP BY d.Dnumber, p.Pnumber
ORDER BY d.Dnumber, total_hours DESC

WITH dept_proj_hours AS (
    SELECT e.Dno AS dept_no,
           w.Pno AS proj_no,
           SUM(w.Hours) AS total_hours
    FROM "works_on" w
    JOIN "employee" e ON w.Essn = e.Ssn
    GROUP BY e.Dno, w.Pno
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT dept_no,
           proj_no,
           total_hours,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept_no ORDER BY total_hours DESC) AS rn
    FROM dept_proj_hours
)
SELECT p."Pname" AS project_name
FROM ranked r
JOIN "project" p ON r.proj_no = p."Pnumber"
WHERE r.rn = 1;

questions.nlq: Could you tell me the names of employees who have worked on all projects in all departments?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean the employees who have worked on every project that every department works on (the projects that are common to all departments).
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH common_projects AS (
    SELECT w.Pno
    FROM works_on w
    JOIN employee e ON w.Essn = e.Ssn
    GROUP BY w.Pno
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.Dno) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Dnumber) FROM department)
)
SELECT e.Fname, e.Lname
FROM employee e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM common_projects cp
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM works_on w
        WHERE w.Essn = e.Ssn AND w.Pno = cp.Pno
    )
);

meanings.hidden_knowledge: I mean, for each department, the employees who have worked on every project that department works on (i.e., each department's own projects).
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT e.Fname || ' ' || e.Lname AS employee_name
FROM employee e
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM department d
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT wo.Essn, p.Dnum, COUNT(DISTINCT wo.Pno) AS worked_cnt
        FROM works_on wo
        JOIN project p ON wo.Pno = p.Pnumber
        GROUP BY wo.Essn, p.Dnum
    ) w ON d.Dnumber = w.Dnum AND w.Essn = e.Ssn
    WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project p2 WHERE p2.Dnum = d.Dnumber) > COALESCE(w.worked_cnt, 0)
);
